title: Montana Lady Griz finalize roster for 2026-27 women's basketball season - Big Sky Times
text:
The Montana Lady Grizzlies women’s basketball team has completed its roster for the upcoming 2026-27 season, head coach Nate Harris announced on May 20. The team will return six players from last year, add four incoming freshmen signed in November, and welcome five new transfers.
This development is significant as it marks a major step in Harris’s efforts to rebuild the program after finishing last season with a record of 9-22 and eighth place in the Big Sky Conference. The mix of returning athletes, new freshmen, and experienced transfers aims to strengthen both the depth and competitiveness of the squad.
“It’s a very obvious challenge when you have a nearly equal split with three different groups, but it’s also exciting. All three groups will challenge the others,” said Nate Harris about integrating returners, freshmen, and transfers. “At the end of the day, it’s our job to make sure those groups become a very successful group as a whole, that they become a team.”
Among those joining Montana are Dominique Nesland from High Point University; Shay Shippen from Columbia; Paige Lofing from Gonzaga; Kennedy Moore from Wake Forest; and Alyssa Blanck from Utah. Each brings experience at high-performing programs or standout high school careers. Returning players include seniors Kennedy Gillette and Aby Shubert; juniors Jocelyn Land and Avery Waddington; sophomores Ava Cossette and Rae Ehrman.
Harris said his focus during recruiting was on adding length, athleticism, efficiency on offense, and aggressiveness on defense: “To accomplish the things that are expected from Lady Griz Basketball, we had to get longer and we had to get more athletic… We had to answer those questions first. Is this somebody who pushes the envelope for us in terms of their effort, their athleticism, their length?”
He highlighted Nesland’s winning background: “Dom is a winner… She will help us in a multitude of ways on the floor… She is explosive downhill, physical defensively and a tremendous rebounder for her position.” On Shippen’s arrival he said: “She is a winner and super competitive… She just knows how to score the basketball.” Regarding Lofing’s return to Montana after playing at Gonzaga he added: “We’re tickled to get a player the quality of Paige… We’re excited to see what she can accomplish in a Lady Griz jersey.” For Moore he stated: “If you start games in the ACC you’re the real deal… I fully expect her to be one of most athletic players in Big Sky.” Of Blanck he commented: “She is excited to compete… We think she is somebody who can make an impact in Big Sky.”
The entire roster will assemble mid-June for summer workouts as preparations begin for next season. Looking ahead Harris concluded: “I think all five (of these transfers) could have been best player on most Big Sky teams and we have them all on same team.”
